newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes draw thin refiner interest.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes draw thin refiner interest.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes attracted limited refiner interest on Monday because of an uneconomic transAtlantic arbitrage and ample domestic supplies.
"At $1.15 (West Texas Intermediate/Brent), the arbitrage is about 20 cents away from being profitable," an East Coast trader said, noting however nominal delivered Brent levels.
First-half October Brent cargoes were assessed around Nov WTI plus 10-20 cents cif.
But traders said Louisiana crudes were more economic at 30 cents premium over WTI/Cushing, and refiners were showing a preference for domestic grades at the moment.
Nigerian Forcados and similar distillate-rich grades were also attracting better interest than Brent, although Forcados at Nov WTI plus 60-70 cents cif was considered costly.
Regional crudes were also available for Oct, with premiums against WTI holding around firmer levels.
Oriente was pegged at WTI minus $1.80-90 cif for Oct into the U.S. Gulf, and Cano Limon at WTI minus $1.55-60 fob.
In late U.S. trade, a second Brent cargo done on an fob basis was reported traded Oct Brent minus 45 cents for late Sept, in contrast to an earlier deal at Nov parity for an early Oct cargo.
In the U.S. after market, intermonth Brent for Oct/Nov moved at 43 cents, slightly firmer than morning trade.
Nov/Dec Brent traded between 44 and 47 cents.
Outright partials moved between $22.40-43 a barrel, up from the IPE Nov Brent crude settlement at $22.27.
